newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-WORK ON LENS WORLD CUP STADIUM BEHIND SCHEDULE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WORK ON LENS WORLD CUP STADIUM BEHIND SCHEDULE.

text.p: Lens' Bollaert stadium, which is being refurbished for the 1998 World Cup finals, could fail to make the deadline for the four-team Tournoi de France warm-up event this June.

The stadium, currently under a one-match ban by the French Football Federation (FFF) after a linesman was knocked out by a water bottle thrown by a spectator, is scheduled to host the match between world champions Brazil and England on June 10.
Work on the stadium was already 40 days behind schedule when in January the architect and another official involved in the alterations were put under investigation for possible fraud.

Following a visit of World Cup organising committee (CFO) officials to Lens on Friday, a decision on whether to keep the stadium on the Tournoi calendar could be taken at a meeting early next week of the FFF and CFO.
If Lens is ruled out, the Brazil-England match could go to Parc des Princes in Paris or Nantes, both of which are already staging Tournoi de France matches.
